flows.title: Someone messages an agent on Slack

steps.note: A person sends a message to the agent in Slack (or Telegram, WhatsApp…).
The gateway's Slack connection receives it and works out which agent it's for.
The gateway checks the agent is allowed to answer and starts a chat session.
The agent runner loads the agent, asks the AI model and calls any tools it needs.
The AI model writes the reply.
The usage is recorded so the customer can be billed.

flows.title: A developer builds an agent with the assistant

steps.note: The developer types what they want in the builder chat; the gateway receives it.
The gateway checks who they are and streams the chat to the assistant.
The assistant plans the agent team, writes tools and picks settings.
It saves the new agent and its tools to the main server.
The main server stores the agent and its new version.
Every model and tool call produces a usage event on a queue.
The usage tracker reads the events and works out the cost with prices from the main server.
The main server receives usage and bills it.
Its billing logic charges the customer's wallet through the payments service.
Payments takes it from the wallet and credits the developer's earnings.
